(sd-pam).description: Helper thread of 'systemd --user' that holds the PAM session open for your login. Normal; one per user session. Killing it logs you out.

ModemManager.description: Manages mobile broadband modems (USB dongles, embedded WWAN). Idle on systems without one but loaded by default.

NetworkManager.description: Primary network configuration daemon — manages wired/wifi/VPN connections via the kernel and wpa_supplicant.

Xvnc.description: TigerVNC X server — serves an X11 display over the VNC protocol. One per active VNC display (:1, :2, ...).

accounts-daemon.description: AccountsService — exposes user account metadata (name, picture, last login) over D-Bus to the login screen and session.

agent.description: Generic name — on this Oracle Linux host it's the main Oracle Cloud Agent binary (under oracle-cloud-agent). Verify via Cmdline / parent chain.

agetty.description: Getty for a virtual console — runs login prompts on tty1..tty6. One per active VT. Safe to leave alone.

at-spi-bus-laun.description: at-spi-bus-launcher — starts the accessibility (AT-SPI) D-Bus instance.

at-spi2-registr.description: at-spi2-registryd — registers accessible apps so screen readers (Orca) can introspect the UI.

atd.description: at(1) daemon — runs one-shot jobs scheduled with `at`. Idle if you don't use it.

auditd.description: Linux audit daemon — receives audit events from the kernel and writes them to /var/log/audit. Required by SELinux/audit rules.

avahi-daemon.description: Zeroconf / mDNS / DNS-SD — advertises and discovers services (printers, file shares) on the local network.

bash.description: GNU Bash shell. Interactive instances belong to MINE; long-running ones with no TTY are usually wrappers around a backgrounded command (check Cmdline).

catatonit.description: Tiny init process used as PID 1 inside Podman containers — reaps zombies and forwards signals. Seeing it on the host means you're looking through into a container's process tree.

chronyd.description: NTP time-sync daemon (chrony). Usually replaces ntpd on modern RHEL/Oracle Linux. Should report tiny drift.

claude.description: Claude Code CLI — Anthropic's terminal coding assistant.

colord.description: Color management daemon — stores ICC profiles for monitors/printers and serves them to apps.

conmon.description: Container monitor (Podman/CRI-O). Supervises one container's main process: reaps it, pipes stdout/stderr, and exposes an attach socket. One per running container.

crond.description: cron — runs scheduled jobs from /etc/cron* and per-user crontabs.

cupsd.description: CUPS — the system print server. Holds the printer list and the print spooler.

dbus-broker.description: High-performance D-Bus message broker (replaces the older dbus-daemon). One instance for the system bus and one per user session.

dbus-broker-lau.description: dbus-broker-launch — sets up the bus environment and launches dbus-broker. Sits as the broker's parent.

dconf-service.description: dconf backend — serves GNOME's binary settings database. Activated on first read; should be cheap.

dtprobed.description: DTrace probe enumeration daemon — registers USDT probes from running binaries with the DTrace kernel module. Oracle Linux's DTrace stack.

entrypoint.description: Generic name — a binary the container image declared as ENTRYPOINT. Identify by Cmdline and parent (usually conmon/catatonit).

esbuild.description: Fast JS/TS bundler written in Go. Usually spawned by a Node dev server or bundler (Vite, tsup) as a long-lived child.

falcon-fxpredic.description: CrowdStrike Falcon ML helper (fx-predict) — runs on-host inference for falcon-sensor's behavioural detections. Comm truncated to 15 chars.

falcon-sensor.description: CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint security agent. Kernel-mode sensor — ships telemetry to Falcon Cloud and enforces policy. Standard on managed enterprise / Oracle Linux hosts.

falcon-sensor-b.description: CrowdStrike Falcon sensor BPF helper — falcon-sensor-bpf, used for kernel-level event collection via eBPF.

falcond.description: CrowdStrike Falcon EDR sensor — endpoint detection & response agent. Sends telemetry to CrowdStrike cloud and applies prevention policy.

firefox.description: Firefox browser main process. Sandbox children (Web Content, Socket Process, RDD Process, Utility Process, ...) appear under it in tree mode.

firewalld.description: Dynamic firewall daemon — manages nftables/iptables rules with zones. The standard firewall on RHEL/Oracle Linux.

flatpak-session.description: flatpak-session-helper — runs autostart hooks and exposes host capabilities to Flatpak apps in your session.

fluentd.description: Open-source log collector / forwarder. Tails files or sockets and ships log records to backends. On Oracle Linux often part of the OCI Logging Analytics agent.

fusermount.description: Helper that mounts FUSE filesystems on behalf of unprivileged users. Brief invocation; long-lived ones are unusual.

fusermount3.description: FUSE mount helper (FUSE 3 variant). Same role as fusermount.

fwupd.description: Firmware update daemon (LVFS). Discovers BIOS/SSD/NIC firmware updates and stages them; activated on demand by GNOME Software / fwupdmgr.

gjs.description: GNOME JavaScript runtime (SpiderMonkey). Used by GNOME Shell extensions and some desktop tools.

gnome-keyring-d.description: gnome-keyring-daemon — stores passwords, SSH keys, and PKCS#11 secrets, unlocked by your login.

gnome-screensho.description: GNOME Screenshot tool (gnome-screenshot) — invoked when the user takes a screenshot. Transient. Comm truncated to 15 chars.

gnome-session-b.description: gnome-session-binary — orchestrates startup of all GNOME components (shell, panels, daemons) for a login session.

gnome-session-c.description: gnome-session-ctl / -checkpoint — helper invoked by gnome-session-binary at session boundaries.

gnome-shell.description: GNOME Shell — the desktop's window manager + UI, written as a Mutter plugin. CPU/RAM hog if extensions misbehave.

gnome-shell-cal.description: gnome-shell-calendar-server — fetches calendar events from Evolution data server for the shell's clock/calendar widget.

gnome-software.description: GNOME Software — the GUI app store/updater. Usually idle but periodically wakes to refresh package metadata.

gnome-terminal-.description: gnome-terminal-server — a single process backs all gnome-terminal windows/tabs in your session.

goa-daemon.description: GNOME Online Accounts — central D-Bus service holding credentials for accounts (Google, Nextcloud, IMAP) shared across GNOME apps.

goa-identity-se.description: goa-identity-service — companion to goa-daemon, manages enterprise identities (Kerberos / IPA).

gomon.description: Oracle Cloud Agent's Go-based monitoring binary, harvesting host metrics for the OCI Monitoring service.

gssproxy.description: GSSAPI proxy — performs Kerberos credential operations on behalf of services like NFS, isolating keytabs.

gvfsd.description: Master GNOME VFS daemon — the parent process under which the gvfsd-* protocol backends are spawned on demand.

ibus-daemon.description: IBus bus daemon — coordinates input-method engines and x11/portal bridges.

ibus-dconf.description: ibus-dconf — exposes IBus settings stored in dconf.

ibus-engine-sim.description: ibus-engine-simple — fallback IBus engine that handles compose-key sequences.

ibus-extension-.description: ibus-extension-gtk3 — GTK3 helper that handles IBus preedit popups and language switchers.

ibus-portal.description: ibus-portal — D-Bus portal so sandboxed (Flatpak) apps can use IBus.

ibus-x11.description: ibus-x11 — bridges IBus to X11 client apps that don't speak the IBus protocol natively.

irqbalance.description: Distributes hardware interrupt affinity across CPUs to spread load. Adjusts /proc/irq/*/smp_affinity over time.

iscsid.description: open-iscsi initiator daemon — maintains iSCSI sessions to remote storage targets.

kauditd.description: Kernel-side audit message broker — relays audit records from the kernel netlink socket to userspace auditd.

kcompactd0.description: Kernel memory compaction daemon — defragments physical memory so larger contiguous allocations succeed.

kdevtmpfs.description: Kernel devtmpfs helper — creates /dev nodes from device-add events before udev takes over.

khugepaged.description: Transparent Huge Pages daemon — opportunistically collapses 4K pages into 2M hugepages in the background.

khungtaskd.description: Kernel hung-task detector — fires a warning (or panic) when a task stays in uninterruptible sleep too long.

ksmd.description: Kernel Same-page Merging daemon — deduplicates identical pages across processes (mostly useful for KVM hosts).

ksplice.description: Oracle Ksplice live patching agent — applies kernel and userspace security fixes without reboot. Default on Oracle Linux.

kswapd0.description: Kernel swap daemon — pages anonymous memory out to swap when free memory falls below a watermark. One per NUMA node.

kthreadd.description: Kernel thread daemon (PID 2) — parent of every kernel thread. The kernel asks it to spawn new threads.

lsmd.description: libstoragemgmt daemon — vendor-neutral API for managing storage arrays (HBAs, SAN). Idle unless lsmcli is used.

nautilus.description: GNOME Files — the desktop file manager. Also draws the desktop icons in older configurations.

nm-dispatcher.description: NetworkManager dispatcher — runs hook scripts in /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d on connection events. Mostly idle.

node.description: Node.js runtime. Inspect Cmdline for the entry script (could be a dev server, electron app helper, language server, etc.).

oci-falcon.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure agent plugin — Falcon, gathers compute metrics for the OCI Monitoring service. Part of oracle-cloud-agent.

oci-fams.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure agent plugin — FAMS (Fleet Application Management Service) for patching and lifecycle ops.

oci-wlp.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure agent plugin — WLP (WebLogic Plugin) integration; only relevant if you use Oracle WebLogic on this host.

ollama.description: Local LLM runtime — serves models like Llama / Mistral over an HTTP API on localhost:11434.

oom_reaper.description: Out-of-memory reaper — asynchronously reclaims memory from a process the OOM killer just terminated, so the kernel doesn't have to wait for natural exit.

osqueryd.description: osquery daemon (Meta open-source) — exposes OS state as SQL tables and runs scheduled queries. Often deployed for fleet visibility / EDR.

p11-kit-server.description: PKCS#11 (smart card / HSM) bus server — lets multiple apps share access to crypto tokens.

packagekitd.description: PackageKit daemon — distro-agnostic D-Bus API for software install/update/query. GNOME Software talks to this rather than dnf directly.

pipewire.description: Modern audio/video routing daemon. Replaces PulseAudio + JACK; one per user.

pipewire-pulse.description: PulseAudio compatibility layer for PipeWire — speaks the PA protocol so legacy apps still work.

pmcd.description: Performance Co-Pilot collector daemon — runs PMDAs and exposes metrics over the network for pmlogger / pmie / pminfo.

pmie.description: Performance Co-Pilot inference engine — evaluates rule-based alerts over PCP metrics.

pmlogger.description: Performance Co-Pilot metric logger — periodically samples PCP metrics into archive files for later replay.

pmlogger_check.description: Performance Co-Pilot helper — periodic health check on pmlogger archive recording. Run from cron / systemd timer.

pmlogger_daily.description: Performance Co-Pilot helper — daily roll-over of pmlogger archives (rotates and compresses yesterday's metrics).

pmlogger_janito.description: Performance Co-Pilot pmlogger_janitor — prunes old pmlogger archives per retention policy. Comm truncated to 15 chars.

pmpause.description: PCP archive helper — invoked by pmlogger to atomically pause/rotate archives.

polkitd.description: PolicyKit daemon — gatekeeper for privileged operations requested over D-Bus (e.g. systemctl, GNOME settings). Decides whether to prompt for auth.

pool_workqueue_release.description: Releases unused per-CPU workqueue pools when the kernel decides they aren't needed anymore.

postmaster.description: PostgreSQL primary server process. Each per-connection backend is a child of postmaster. Multiple postmasters means multiple PG clusters.

python3.description: CPython 3 interpreter. The PID alone doesn't tell you what it's doing — check Cmdline for the script being run.

rpcbind.description: RPC port mapper. Tells RPC clients (notably NFS) what port a given RPC program is listening on. Only useful if you use NFS / NIS.

rsyslogd.description: Classic syslog daemon. On systemd systems often coexists with journald, taking input from /dev/log or imjournal.

rtkit-daemon.description: RealtimeKit — grants real-time scheduling to client processes (PipeWire, PulseAudio) under policy limits.

ruby.description: Ruby interpreter — check Cmdline for the actual script. On this system frequently used by Performance Co-Pilot's pmrep tooling.

runcommand.description: Oracle Cloud Agent plugin that executes commands sent through OCI Run Command. Idle until a job arrives.

sedispatch.description: SELinux audit-dispatch — forwards SELinux AVC denials from auditd to setroubleshoot for human-readable analysis.

sleep.description: /usr/bin/sleep — pauses for N seconds. If long-lived and detached, it's almost always part of a shell loop or a 'wait' in a script.

ssh-agent.description: Caches your decrypted SSH private keys for the session, so you aren't prompted for the passphrase on every git/ssh.

sshd.description: OpenSSH daemon. The system-level instance listens for incoming SSH; a per-connection child handles each session and is owned by the connecting user.

sssd_kcm.description: SSSD's Kerberos Credential Manager — stores Kerberos tickets in a centralized cache instead of per-process files.

sudo.description: sudo — running an authorized command as another user (usually root). The Cmdline reveals what's actually being executed.

systemd.description: PID 1 init system; manages services, mounts, sockets, login sessions, and the boot/shutdown lifecycle. Also runs as 'systemd --user' for per-user service management.

systemd-hostnam.description: systemd-hostnamed — D-Bus service that exposes/changes the hostname. Activated on demand; should be idle.

systemd-journal.description: systemd-journald — collects logs from the kernel, syslog, and all services into the structured systemd journal. Read with journalctl.

systemd-logind.description: Tracks user logins and seats; manages session lifecycles, idle/lock state, and inhibitor locks (e.g. 'don't suspend during update').

systemd-timedat.description: systemd-timedated — D-Bus interface for time/date settings (timezone, RTC mode). Started on demand by timedatectl. Comm truncated to 15 chars.

systemd-udevd.description: Device manager — listens for kernel uevents and applies udev rules to create /dev nodes, set perms, load firmware, and run device-add hooks.

tuned.description: Dynamic system tuning daemon — applies a profile (throughput-performance, balanced, latency-performance) that adjusts CPU/IO/network knobs.

tuned-ppd.description: tuned's power-profiles-daemon shim — exposes a power-profiles-daemon-compatible D-Bus API on top of tuned.

udisksd.description: Storage device management over D-Bus — mount/unmount/format removable disks, manage partitions. Backs file-manager mount actions.

unifiedmonitori.description: unifiedmonitoringagent — Oracle's unified monitoring agent (often Fluentd-based) that ships logs and metrics from this host to OCI services.

updater.description: Oracle Cloud Agent self-updater — checks for and applies new agent versions.

upowerd.description: Power and battery info via D-Bus. Feeds laptop battery indicators and triggers low-power events.

vncsession.description: TigerVNC vncsession — launched by the vncserver@ systemd unit; sets up the user environment and execs Xvnc for that display.

watchdogd.description: Kernel watchdog daemon — pets the hardware/software watchdog timer so the system doesn't auto-reset.

wireplumber.description: PipeWire session and policy manager — decides routing, default sinks, device priorities.

wlp-agent.ext.description: Oracle Cloud Agent's WebLogic plugin extension binary, spawned by oci-wlp.

wpa_supplicant.description: Implements WPA/WPA2/WPA3 authentication for wifi (and sometimes wired 802.1X). Driven by NetworkManager.

xdg-desktop-por.description: xdg-desktop-portal — main XDG portal: file chooser, screenshot, notification, etc., on behalf of sandboxed apps. Backends (-gnome, -gtk) implement the UI.

xdg-document-po.description: xdg-document-portal — exposes a per-app FUSE mount in /run/user/UID/doc so sandboxed apps can access user-selected files without filesystem access.

xdg-permission-.description: xdg-permission-store — persists per-app permission decisions ("always allow camera for X") for the portals.

xinit.description: Starts an X server and a single client (typically a session manager). Used here to bring up the GNOME session inside the VNC X server.

patterns.description: Kernel workqueue thread — runs deferred work for some kernel subsystem (the suffix names it: e.g. -events, -xfs-sync, -kblockd). Created and destroyed by the kernel as needed; presence is normal.
Per-CPU softirq handler. Runs network/timer/RCU softirqs that overflowed the interrupt context. One per CPU. Heavy CPU here means the system is taking a lot of soft interrupts.
Per-CPU stop-machine helper used to migrate tasks between CPUs and run synchronization fences. One per CPU. Should sit at 0% almost always.
Per-CPU CPU hot-plug coordinator. Drives the bring-up and tear-down of a logical CPU. Idle on stable systems.
Per-CPU idle-injection thread. Used by thermal throttling to force CPUs idle when they get too hot.
Threaded interrupt handler — the kernel runs the bottom half of an IRQ in this thread. Suffix names the device or driver (e.g. irq/9-acpi, irq/24-aerdrv for PCIe AER).

Read-Copy-Update machinery. Reclaims memory freed by RCU readers. Multiple variants exist (preempt, tasks, exp_gp, ...). Idle most of the time; load here usually means heavy RCU usage in some subsystem.
Per-SCSI-host error handler thread. Sits idle until a command times out or fails; activity here usually means a flaky disk.
XFS Active Item List Daemon — flushes XFS journal items to disk for the named device. One per mounted XFS filesystem.
Journaling Block Device v2 — handles ext4 (and ocfs2) journal commits for the named device.
Broadcom NetXtreme II iSCSI offload helper thread. Only relevant on systems using bnx2i hardware iSCSI; otherwise idle.
GNOME Settings Daemon helper. Each gsd-* binary handles one slice of desktop configuration (color, power, keyboard, media-keys, etc.). Started by the user's GNOME session.
GNOME Virtual Filesystem backend. Implements pseudo-filesystems exposed to apps over D-Bus (network shares, trash, metadata, dnssd, etc.).
GNOME VFS volume monitor — watches a class of removable/online storage (udisks2, mtp, gphoto2, goa) and surfaces it to the file manager.
IBus input method framework. Handles non-Latin / CJK / IME text input; ibus-daemon orchestrates engines (ibus-engine-*) and the X11/portal bridges.
XDG desktop portal — D-Bus interface that lets sandboxed apps (Flatpak, Snap) request host capabilities (file access, screenshots, notifications) under user consent.
GNOME Evolution data server component. Backs calendars, address books, alarms, and account sources for Evolution and any GNOME app that consumes them.
Performance Co-Pilot Metric Domain Agent. Each pmda* exports metrics from one subsystem (linux, kvm, xfs, proc, root, dm) to pmcd for collection.
